prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1260; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss from insured by phone. Low-speed head-on collision at an intersection, both vehicles drivable but insured reports neck stiffness. Opened bodily injury and property damage exposures. Tow and rental questions pending.

Entry 2: Claimant represented by counsel as of today. Letter of representation received. All further contact to go through the attorney's office. Requested medical authorization and prior records through counsel.

Entry 3: Spoke with defense-side counsel regarding liability. Police report notes the other driver crossed the center line on approach. Liability appears clear in favor of insured. Photos of both vehicles reviewed; damage consistent with reported speed.

Entry 4: Received treatment summary from claimant's physician. Diagnosis listed as cervical and lumbar strain, conservative care recommended, follow-up in several weeks. No imaging ordered at this time. Reserve reviewed and adjusted for medical specials.

Entry 5: Counsel's office confirmed claimant is still in physical therapy. Demand package expected once treatment concludes. Diary set for follow-up with counsel. Property damage estimate finalized and sent to repair shop for supplement review.
